Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Initial submissions repeatedly failed because priority and ship_country were invalid or missing. This occurred for Eli Okafor, Bo Reyes, Cy Okafor, Dee Okafor, and Eli Sato.
- Retrying on attempt 2 with corrected priority and ship_country was accepted in every observed case.
- Do not infer priority solely from front-desk comments such as “ordinary priority”; ensure the submitted value matches the accepted format.
- Preserve customer, email, order_date, and qty from the source record while correcting only invalid/missing fields.
- These are emailed or phone-transcribed orders; carefully parse the source text and verify all six required fields before submission.
- Attempts allow up to 3 tries; use the next attempt after rejection rather than creating an unrelated order.

Order intake notes:
- Form versions 1 and 2 both list the same six required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every field against the accepted format before submission. Recent failures involved:
  - priority alone (Bo Okafor)
  - ship_country alone (Dee Okafor)
  - priority plus qty (Eli Okafor)
  - qty plus ship_country (Eli Okafor, Ada Okafor)
  - priority, qty, and ship_country (Eli Okafor, Ada Okafor)
- Do not infer priority from comments such as “ordinary priority” or “marked ordinary priority”; determine the exact accepted value.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, and front-desk transcriptions. Verify all six fields, especially numeric qty and country, before submitting.
- Preserve cust, email, order_date, and source qty unless the source or validation requires correction; do not substitute values based on assumptions.
- Earlier cases succeeded on attempt 2 after correcting priority and ship_country, but recent retries still failed. Never assume a corrected retry will pass.
- Use the next attempt on the same order after rejection; do not create an unrelated order.
- There are at most 3 attempts. If validation remains unresolved, the record goes to manual review, as occurred for ORD-5110–ORD-5112, ORD-5113–ORD-5115, and ORD-5116–ORD-5118.

Order intake notes:
- Form versions 1 and 2 require the same six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every field and accepted format before submission. Recent rejections involved:
  - priority alone (Bo Okafor, Cy Sato, Eli Okafor, Ada Reyes, Eli Okafor)
  - ship_country alone (Dee Okafor)
  - priority plus qty (Eli Okafor)
  - qty plus ship_country (Eli Okafor, Ada Okafor)
  - priority, qty, and ship_country (Eli Okafor, Ada Okafor)
  - priority plus ship_country (Dee Okafor)
- Do not infer priority from “ordinary priority” or similar comments. Determine the exact accepted value.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, handwritten, portal, and front-desk transcriptions. Verify all six fields, especially numeric qty and ship_country.
- Preserve cust, email, order_date, and source qty unless explicit source data or validation requires correction. Never substitute values by assumption.
- A retry can succeed after correcting only priority (ORD-5122/5123, ORD-5124/5125, ORD-5127/5128), but never assume a correction will pass. Recheck every field before retrying.
- Use the next attempt on the same order after rejection; do not create an unrelated order.
- There are at most 3 attempts. If unresolved, stop after the final rejection and allow manual review (ORD-5110–ORD-5118 and ORD-5120–ORD-5121).

Order intake notes:
- Form versions 1, 2, and 3 require the same six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every field and exact accepted format before submission. Recent failures show:
  - priority alone; ship_country alone; priority plus qty; qty plus ship_country; priority plus ship_country; and combinations of priority, qty, and ship_country.
  - order_date is also format-sensitive: ISO YYYY-MM-DD was rejected in recent records, and MM/DD/YYYY was likewise rejected. Do not retry date formats by assumption; determine the exact accepted format from validation/source guidance.
- Do not infer priority from “ordinary priority” or similar wording. Determine the exact accepted value.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, handwritten, portal, and front-desk transcriptions. Verify all six fields, especially numeric qty, ship_country, priority, and order_date.
- Preserve cust, email, order_date, and source qty unless explicit source data or validation requires correction. Never substitute values by assumption.
- A retry may succeed after correcting only priority, but recent records required attention to both order_date and priority. Recheck every field before retrying.
- Use the next attempt on the same order after rejection; do not create an unrelated order.
- There are at most 3 attempts. If unresolved, stop after the final rejection and allow manual review. Recent ORD-5130–ORD-5139 failures confirm that exhausted records proceed to manual review.

Order intake notes:
- Form versions 1–4 require the same six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate all six fields and exact formats before submission. Preserve source values unless validation or explicit source data requires correction.
- Confirmed accepted date format: DD/MM/YYYY with slashes (e.g., 22/10/2026; 09/10/2026 passed date validation). Rejected formats include ISO YYYY-MM-DD, DD-MM-YYYY, and textual dates such as 09-Oct-2026. Do not assume other formats.
- Priority is exact-value sensitive. “Ordinary priority” and similar wording are not valid values; determine the accepted value from authoritative validation/source guidance. Recent failures commonly involve priority alone or priority with date errors.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, handwritten, portal, email, and front-desk transcriptions. Verify customer, email, numeric qty, ship_country, priority, and DD/MM/YYYY order_date. Do not “correct” names or values by assumption.
- After rejection, recheck every field, not only the listed invalid field; recent successes required correcting date and priority together. Retry the same order, never an unrelated order.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the final rejection, stop and allow manual review. ORD-5130–ORD-5140, ORD-5145, and ORD-5148 demonstrate exhausted records proceed to manual review.

Order intake notes:
- Form versions 1–4 require exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every field and exact format before submission. Preserve source values unless validation or explicit authoritative data requires correction; never “correct” names or values by assumption.
- Accepted order_date format is DD/MM/YYYY with slashes (e.g., 22/10/2026, 09/10/2026). Reject ISO, hyphenated, and textual dates; do not assume other formats.
- Priority is exact-value sensitive. “Ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary,” and similar intake wording are invalid. Recent batches ORD-5150 through ORD-5159 repeatedly failed on priority alone, including after resubmission. Determine the accepted priority value from authoritative validation/source guidance; do not retry an unchanged invalid priority.
- Carefully parse voicemail, phone, handwritten, portal, email, and front-desk transcriptions. Verify cust, email, numeric qty, ship_country, priority, and date.
- After rejection, recheck all six fields, even when only one invalid field is listed. Correct date and priority together if warranted, but only using authoritative evidence.
- Retry the same order only; never substitute another order. Maximum 3 attempts. After the final rejection, stop and allow manual review. ORD-5130–ORD-5140, ORD-5145, ORD-5148, ORD-5150–ORD-5157 demonstrate exhausted records proceed to manual review.
- ORD-5158 is at attempt 2 of 3 and still has an unresolved priority failure; ORD-5159 is also at attempt 2 of 3 with priority failure. Do not spend the final attempt without identifying the valid priority.
